chapter: Tiny Bradshaw, Teddy Hill and Europe
title: Myth that musicians lose their playing in Europe: Teddy Hill, Armstrong, Hawkins
summary: He had turned down earlier Europe offers; Teddy Hill claimed Europe ruined players, but Procope points to Louis Armstrong coming back playing better than ever.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yes, it was. Well, you see, before

that I had, you know, two or three offers before, but I just wouldn't want to go because I liked what I was doing at the time, you know. I was exposed to all this music business, which I really wanted to do, so I could, you know, better myself. And I didn't think running off to Europe would do me any good. And I remember one time when Teddy Hill, he called a rehearsal at the Moulin Rouge, it was, and I remember him making a statement. He said -- you know, all the fellows, they didn't want to rehearse. They were having a ball in Paris, you know, going on tours, the Eiffel Tower and all that sort of thing, the bawdy houses and all that sort of thing. And so Teddy Hill said, "That's why musicians who come to Europe and they come back to America, they can't play nothing." I said, "Teddy, the musicians who come back to American and can't play nothing, they couldn't play nothing when they left." See, he couldn't conceive of that. You know. And that was the thinking at the time, because I remember when Louis Armstrong came -- went, rather, to Europe. You know, all the time he spent, sort of a lengthy time. I don't know how long it was, in Europe. And all the trumpet players in Harlem, they were readying themselves, like they were all telling each other, "We're going to get Louis when he comes back." You know, and I would say, "Get him what? You mean you're going to blow him away?" "Oh, yeah, he won't be able to play nothing." I don't know where they got that from. And lo and behold, Louis came back and he played up
at the Savoy, and Louis was playing more than ever, and you couldn't find those trumpet players. That's true. So I don't know where that idea came from.
Yeah. Well, did they think Coleman Hawkins had had it when he came back?
